description: Controlled vocabulary for the reading-15 literature knowledge graph. Node and relation types are closed lists; a relation outside the list is kept but flagged relation_known=false. v1.1.0 adds contains and reports_metric, the surface_variant merge rule and the co_occurrence strength used by the deterministic baseline.
direction_rule: deterministic layer: the nearest entity left of the trigger is the source, the nearest entity right of it is the target; passive patterns may swap them; a comparative such as 'higher A than B' takes the entity before 'higher' as source and the entity after 'than' as target; endpoint types are checked per relation

node_types.researcher: a person or author named in the material
node_types.material: a physical material, sample, compound, catalyst or reagent
node_types.method: a method, technique, instrument or procedure
node_types.task: a research task, reaction, benchmark, dataset or problem setting
node_types.metric: a measured quantity, performance metric or indicator
node_types.conclusion: a finding or claim stated by the paper
node_types.concept: a concept that does not fit the other types
node_types.other: a real entity whose type is not in this schema

improves.definition: source improves, raises or reduces target

supports.definition: source evidence supports a target claim

causes.definition: source causes or leads to target

is_a.definition: source is a kind of target

contains.definition: source is composed of / contains target

reports_metric.definition: source reports a measured value for the target metric; values stay doc-scoped and are never averaged across papers

co_occurs.definition: deterministic fallback: same paragraph; a relation is explicitly NOT asserted

other.definition: a real relation whose type is not in this schema

merge_rules.same_surface: identical normalised surface (case, hyphen, space and slash insensitive)
merge_rules.acronym_definition: the material itself defines acronym and full form (Full Name (ABC) pattern)
merge_rules.agent_alias: the alias is declared by the agent in nodes.json and matches another node label
merge_rules.surface_variant: the surfaces differ only by a trailing generic head noun (catalyst / sample / reaction / method / system); merged and logged with the full member list and per-member quote
merge_rules.never_merge: different declared types on the same surface are a homonym: the nodes stay separate and the conflict is recorded

strength_levels.strong: explicit verb links both endpoints in one sentence (score 0.9)
strength_levels.moderate: explicit verb present but separated across clauses (score 0.6)
strength_levels.weak: trigger found but the relation is not directly asserted (score 0.35)
strength_levels.co_occurrence: same paragraph only; relation NOT asserted (score 0.2)

evidence_rules.node: an anchor must locate the label in the cited paragraph and the quote must mention the label
evidence_rules.edge: the quote must contain BOTH endpoint labels and be a verbatim substring of the cited paragraph
evidence_rules.condition: an edge condition is attached only when the extracted snippet also appears verbatim in that edge's own quote, so a stray digit from a formula cannot become a condition
evidence_rules.locator: paragraph_id is the publisher/JATS paragraph id; a PDF page is reported only when the material is a real PDF

status_semantics.success: documents read, >=3 nodes and >=3 edges, every node and edge grounded, >=3 executed queries, no dropped claim, inside the time budget - a deterministic baseline that meets this is a SUCCESS
status_semantics.partial: a real degradation occurred: a claim was dropped as unverifiable, fewer than three queries could be executed, or the soft deadline was reached
status_semantics.failed: no readable material at all; the contract shape and the reason are still written
